assets.author: Claude
assets.prompt: A 12 s stereo loop of a crypt's low room tone: brown-tilted noise (rolled off above 420 Hz, high-passed at 28 Hz, part shared and part its own on each side), two narrow hollow stone modes of noise at 176 and 263 Hz, a faint hiss above 1.8 kHz, a very soft drone of sines at 55, 55.25 and 82.5 Hz, the air breathing on a slow whole-cycle swell. Every noise is shaped in the frequency domain over exactly the loop's length and every tone and swell has whole cycles in it, so the loop is periodic and has no seam. RMS -27 dBFS, peak -14 dBFS. The file starts at the point of the loop (a rotation of it) where its Vorbis seam decodes as smoothly as the rest: the step and the curvature across it below the 80th percentile of the decoded loop's own.

assets.author: Claude
assets.prompt: A 1.9 s mono far water drip: a sine ping at 1150 Hz whose pitch rises 55% over 45 ms (a bubble's), decaying over 30 ms, with a soft high tick, convolved with a synthetic crypt reverb (exponentially decaying band-limited noise, RT60 1.5 s, 12 ms pre-delay) mixed wetter than dry, its top dulled above 5.2 kHz, faded to silence. Rendered at peak -9 dBFS; the encoded file peaks at -10.4 dBFS, RMS -29 dBFS.

assets.author: Claude
assets.prompt: A 1.9 s mono far double drip: as the single drip, a lower ping at 820 Hz rising 70%, a second softer ping a third higher 180 ms after it, through the same kind of synthetic crypt reverb, faded to silence. Rendered at peak -9 dBFS; the encoded file peaks at -8.8 dBFS, RMS -27.9 dBFS.

assets.author: Claude
assets.prompt: A 5.5 s mono far rumble through stone: noise low-passed at 95 Hz with a band of growl at 140 Hz, swelling over 1.1 s and settling over 4 s with a slow wobble, nine small grains of grit (short band-passed noise bursts at 600 Hz), through a dark synthetic reverb (RT60 1.6 s), faded to silence. Peak -8 dBFS, RMS -25.5 dBFS.

assets.author: Claude
assets.prompt: A 3.6 s mono gust of wind: white noise through a state-variable band-pass whose centre sweeps from 380 Hz up to 1 kHz and back, swelling in and out over 3.4 s. Peak -10 dBFS.

assets.author: Claude

Periodic by construction (whole cycles of every tone and swell, noise shaped over the loop's length), so it has no seam. RMS -29 dBFS, peak -13 dBFS. The file starts at the point of the loop (a rotation of it) where its Vorbis seam decodes as smoothly as the rest: the step and the curvature across it below the 80th percentile of the decoded loop's own.
